answer: Each claimant may hold only one numbered plot on a communal trial meadow. A uniquely cut jade gauge stays with that plot and is used to measure a single tagged cutting at the start and end of a fixed interval. Peers later reseat the same gauge on the same plant and admit the identity only if the length delta matches the sealed log. A fresh cutting has no accepted interval until one window closes, and the plot and gauge cannot be split across addresses, so every extra identity must grow and re-measure a record no borrowed log can supply.
